Proposed full-read mapping for facts, numbers, citations: Direct fit. The full article teaches claim-by-claim checking against original sources; matching scope/time/units; recomputing figures; separating invented, inaccessible, and irrelevant citations; and recording supported / needs correction / unverified. It includes examples of a real source used to support the wrong date, a unit conversion error, and a stale event schedule. Limitations: Educational guide with synthetic exercises; citation availability alone is not proof, and it recommends human/expert review for high-impact topics.

Proposed full-read mapping for code verification: Direct fit. The full article sets a requirement before examining code, asks for diff/run evidence, tests normal/boundary/invalid inputs, checks the test oracle independently, and separates function-level results from integration/security claims. Its bounded Python example reports 8/8 after a fix and explicitly labels what remains untested. Limitations: Offline teaching example only; no production readiness, full-app security, or broad benchmark claim.

Proposed full-read mapping for RAG versions / citation freshness: Direct fit. Current revision is chosen by an app-owned manifest; candidate citations are untrusted; the gate checks allowlist, current revision, SHA-256 over canonical UTF-8 bytes, byte bounds and exact quote. Old revisions are rejected even when their old hash remains valid. Limitations: The article repeatedly restricts QUOTE_VERIFIED to quote location in the current stored revision, not source truth, publisher identity or entailment. Its implementation/tests are explicitly NOT RUN and the demo is synthetic.

Proposed full-read mapping for permissions / RAG access control: Direct fit. It distinguishes authentication from authorization; uses server-trusted principal/tenant and server-owned policy; checks tenant plus explicit document grant before hydration, reranking or model context; ignores client-supplied grants; and denies by default. It flags upstream search snippets as a separate exposure boundary. Limitations: Mock uses synthetic IDs; tests are written but NOT RUN. It does not authenticate, connect a real index or certify production security; policy freshness/races and provider behavior remain open.

Proposed full-read mapping for approval / action integrity: Direct fit. The full article snapshots action-affecting fields into a fixed-schema fingerprint and binds a scoped, expiring, single-use receipt to that snapshot. The final gate denies changed actions, permanent invalidation after change, scope mismatch, expiry and replay. Limitations: Digest is not identity, signature, authority or consent. The approval fixture is synthetic, ALLOW_MOCK_ONLY has no external effect, and the 19 tests are NOT RUN; durable state, atomicity, concurrency and external-effect reconciliation are out of scope.
ANALYSIS: proposed pedagogical mapping after reading the full public source; difficulty is editorial, not an author or user approval.
